kernels.name: softmax SYCL kernels

launch_config.work_group_size: dynamic: doubles from WARP_SIZE (16) until >= ncols or max_block_size; template specializations at 32/64/128/256/512/1024
launch_config.notes: soft_max_back_f32 uses a fixed work-group of WARP_SIZE (16 on Intel), which is very small. Missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] on fallback forward path (line 293) and backward kernel (line 316) — correctness risk.

memory_patterns.notes: All memory accesses are scalar float. Consecutive threads access consecutive elements (coalesced). No sycl::vec usage for data loads/stores despite vec_aligned_load helper existing in common.hpp.

slm_usage.slm_bytes: (GGML_PAD(ncols, WARP_SIZE) + max(nwarps, WARP_SIZE)) * sizeof(float) for shared path; WARP_SIZE * sizeof(float) for non-shared path
slm_usage.notes: Inter-warp SLM reduction buffer has potential bank conflicts when nreduce > 1 (stride-16 accesses on 16-bank SLM). SLM allocation is larger than CUDA equivalent due to different reduction algorithm requiring nwarps elements vs WARP_SIZE.

reduction_pattern.notes: Two-level reduction: sub-group shuffle (warp_reduce_max/sum) + manual SLM-based inter-warp reduction. Uses 5 barriers (2 for MAX, 3 for SUM) vs CUDA's 2 barriers total (1 per block_reduce call). Does NOT use sycl::reduce_over_group or sycl::joint_reduce. The manual SLM reduction is inlined rather than using a reusable block_reduce utility.

data_types.notes: FP32 throughout is appropriate for softmax numerical stability. Mask input supports both float and sycl::half via template.

math_functions.notes: Good: already uses sycl::native::exp. Minor: could use sycl::native::recip for 1/sum but precision impact may be undesirable.

hot_loops: Column loop (lines 92-103): iterates ncols/block_size times for max computation
Column loop (lines 124-134): iterates ncols/block_size times for exp + sum
Column loop (lines 164-172): iterates ncols/block_size times for normalization
nreduce loop (lines 141-143, 153-155): up to 4 iterations for SLM reduction zeroing/accumulation
loop_analysis.notes: Main column loops have #pragma unroll which works when ncols_template != 0 (compile-time constant). Fallback path (ncols_template == 0) cannot unroll. nreduce loops are NOT unrolled.

DPCT artifact: uses dpct::dim3 instead of sycl::range (lines 272-273, 312-313)
3D nd_range for logically 1D/2D kernel (unnecessary complexity from DPCT migration)
Manual inlined block reduction instead of reusable utility — more barriers than CUDA equivalent
Missing soft_max_f32_parallelize_cols cooperative kernel for large ncols (> 8192)
Missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] on two kernel launch paths — correctness risk
soft_max_back_f32 work-group size is only WARP_SIZE (16 on Intel) — poor occupancy

optimization_opportunities.description: Add missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] attribute on the fallback forward kernel launch (line 293) and backward kernel launch (line 316). Both paths call warp_reduce_max/warp_reduce_sum which rely on sub-group shuffle with assumed width WARP_SIZE. Without the attribute, the runtime may choose a different sub-group size, causing incorrect reductions.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Correctness fix — prevents potential wrong results on hardware where runtime chooses sub-group size != WARP_SIZE
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Add [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] to the lambda in both parallel_for calls at lines 293 and 316 of softmax.cpp
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Low risk — this is adding a constraint that the kernel already implicitly requires

optimization_opportunities.description: Replace manual two-level SLM block reduction (5 barriers) with sycl::reduce_over_group for both MAX and SUM reductions. The current implementation manually inlines a warp-shuffle + SLM inter-warp reduction pattern ported from CUDA, using 5 barriers (2 for MAX, 3 for SUM). sycl::reduce_over_group(item.get_group(), val, op) performs the entire work-group reduction in a single call with optimal barrier usage.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 10-20% speedup from reduced barrier overhead (5 barriers → 0-2 internal barriers managed by runtime) and potentially better reduction tree. Also simplifies code significantly.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Replace lines 105-120 (MAX) with: max_val = sycl::reduce_over_group(item.get_group(), max_val, sycl::maximum<float>()). Replace lines 136-157 (SUM) with: tmp = sycl::reduce_over_group(item.get_group(), tmp, sycl::plus<float>()). Remove the buf_iw SLM allocation for the inter-warp buffer (only keep vals if use_shared). This eliminates the nreduce logic entirely. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 3.4.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Need to verify sycl::reduce_over_group works correctly with all block sizes used (32-1024). Some older oneAPI compiler versions may have bugs with large work-group reductions. Need to verify numerical equivalence with current implementation.

optimization_opportunities.description: Add vectorized memory access (sycl::vec<float, 4>) to the three column loops in soft_max_f32. Currently all loads and stores are scalar float, processing 1 element per thread per iteration. Using vec4 loads would reduce memory transactions by 4x for aligned data.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 20-40% improvement in memory throughput for memory-bound softmax. Softmax is bandwidth-limited (compute intensity ~3-5 ops/byte, well below the 27 ops/byte threshold), so better memory utilization directly translates to speedup.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: For the column loops (lines 92-103, 124-134, 164-172), process 4 elements per iteration using sycl::vec<float, 4> loads. Handle tail elements (ncols % 4 != 0) with scalar fallback. The vec_aligned_load helper in common.hpp line 520 can be used. Need to ensure alignment of x, mask, and dst pointers. For the shared-memory path, vals buffer is already float-aligned since it's SLM. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 2.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Need to handle non-aligned and non-multiple-of-4 ncols correctly. The template specialization for ncols=32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096 are all multiples of 4, so vectorization is safe for those paths. The fallback path needs careful tail handling.

optimization_opportunities.description: Increase soft_max_back_f32 work-group size from WARP_SIZE (16 on Intel) to at least 128 or 256. The current single-warp work-group provides very poor occupancy on Intel Xe2 (only 1 hardware thread per EU). With a larger work-group, multiple warps can cooperate on a single row, improving latency hiding and bandwidth utilization.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 30-50% improvement for backward pass. Larger work-groups better hide memory latency through more concurrent threads per Xe-core. Currently each work-group occupies only 1/8 of an EU's thread capacity.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Change block_dims from (WARP_SIZE, 1, 1) to (256, 1, 1) at line 312. Modify the kernel to use multi-warp reduction: each thread accumulates its partial sum, then use sycl::reduce_over_group instead of single-warp warp_reduce_sum. The column loop stride changes from WARP_SIZE to block_size. Also need to add [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] attribute.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Standard pattern change. The forward kernel already uses larger work-groups successfully. Need to verify backward pass numerical accuracy is maintained.

optimization_opportunities.description: Reduce SLM allocation for inter-warp communication buffer. Current allocation is max(nwarps, WARP_SIZE) floats, which is 256 bytes for 1024-thread work-groups on Intel (nwarps=64). If reduction is replaced with sycl::reduce_over_group (opt_001_002), this buffer is eliminated entirely. Otherwise, restructure the reduction to use only WARP_SIZE elements like the CUDA block_reduce pattern.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 5-10% from reduced SLM pressure allowing more work-groups per Xe-core (higher occupancy). The freed SLM can be used for more vals caching.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: If opt_001_002 is implemented, this is automatically resolved. Otherwise, restructure the SUM reduction to match CUDA's block_reduce pattern: each lane reads shared[lane_id] for lane_id < nwarps, with sentinel 0 for lane_id >= nwarps. This requires only WARP_SIZE elements and 1 barrier per reduction.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Low risk if done carefully. The CUDA version already proves this pattern works correctly.

optimization_opportunities.description: Clean up DPCT migration artifacts: replace this_work_item::get_nd_item<3>() with lambda parameter, replace dpct::dim3 with sycl::range, simplify 3D nd_range to 1D where possible. This improves code maintainability and removes dependency on non-standard SYCL extensions.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: No direct performance improvement, but enables better compiler optimization by making data flow explicit and removes runtime overhead of extension function calls.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: 1. Pass nd_item<3> as function parameter instead of calling this_work_item::get_nd_item<3>() (lines 52, 180). 2. Replace dpct::dim3 with sycl::range<3> (lines 272-273, 312-313). 3. Consider converting to nd_range<1> for the backward kernel which is logically 1D.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Purely mechanical refactoring with no algorithmic changes.

kernels.estimated_current_efficiency: 40-50% — softmax is memory-bound and the current implementation wastes bandwidth through scalar accesses and has excessive barrier overhead from the manual block reduction pattern. The missing sub-group size attributes are a correctness concern.

kernels.name: rope SYCL kernels

launch_config.global_size_expression: ceil_div(ne0, 2*256) work-groups × nr rows; each thread handles one (x0, x1) rotation pair
launch_config.notes: All 4 kernels (rope_norm, rope_neox, rope_multi, rope_vision) use 3D nd_range with SYCL_ROPE_BLOCK_SIZE=256 in dimension 1 only, dimensions 0 and 2 are (1, nr). Missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(16)]] on all 8 kernel launch paths (lines 251, 261, 283, 288, 314, 319, 349, 354). Without this attribute, the compiler may choose sub-group size 32 instead of the native SIMD16 for Xe2.

strided_accesses: rope_neox: reads x[i2+0] and x[i2+n_dims/2] — strided by n_dims/2 (inherent to NeoX half-rotate algorithm)
rope_vision: reads x[ix+0] and x[ix+n_dims] — strided by n_dims
memory_patterns.notes: Within the primary dimension (local_id(1)), adjacent threads access adjacent pairs of elements (i0 = 2*thread_id), so coalesced within a sub-group. sycl::vec<T,2> is used for the passthrough path (lines 61, 101, 140) when i0 >= n_dims, but the HOT rotation computation path uses scalar loads/stores only (lines 74-78, 114-118, 179-184, 223-228). The strided access patterns in neox/multi/vision are algorithmic — they read two halves of the rotation domain that are n_dims/2 apart.

slm_usage.notes: No SLM usage. RoPE is purely element-wise with no data sharing between threads. This is correct.

reduction_pattern.notes: No reductions needed — each thread independently computes one rotation pair.

data_types.notes: All computation is FP32 regardless of input type T. This is appropriate — RoPE involves sin/cos which need FP32 precision. Input is implicitly cast from T to float for computation, results cast back to T for output. Template supports both float and sycl::half inputs.

math_functions.notes: All math functions use standard (full-precision) SYCL versions, NOT sycl::native variants. sycl::pow is called on every thread in the hot path and is the most expensive operation. On Xe2, native::cos and native::sin are ~2-4x faster than standard versions. sycl::pow(base, exp) can be replaced with sycl::native::exp2(sycl::native::log2(base) * exp) for significant speedup. The CUDA version uses cosf/sinf/powf which are already the fast-math equivalents.

loop_analysis.notes: No loops in any kernel. Each thread computes exactly one (x0, x1) rotation pair and returns. rope_multi has an 8-way branch (lines 150-173) for sector-based theta computation, but this is not a loop. No unrolling opportunities.

anti_patterns: Missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(16)]] on all 8 kernel launch paths — suboptimal SIMD width selection on Xe2
3D nd_range with dimension 0 always 1 — DPCT artifact, should be 2D (lines 237-239, 274-276, 302-305, 337-340)
Manual thread indexing (local_range*group+local_id) instead of get_global_id() at lines 46, 52, 86, 92, 128, 132, 196, 200

Unconditional dpct::has_capability_or_fail(fp16) check in rope_norm_sycl and rope_neox_sycl even when T=float (lines 243, 280) — wastes time on device capability query per launch. rope_multi_sycl and rope_vision_sycl correctly guard with if constexpr
Uses standard sycl::cos/sin/pow instead of sycl::native equivalents — significant compute waste on Xe2 for these throughput-bound trig operations
DPCT migration comments still present (lines 246-250, 256-259)

optimization_opportunities.description: Replace sycl::cos and sycl::sin with sycl::native::cos and sycl::native::sin in the rope_yarn function (lines 34-35). These are called for every rotation pair in every RoPE variant. On Xe2, native trig functions are ~2-4x faster than standard precision versions. RoPE precision requirements (position encoding) are well within the accuracy of Intel's native sin/cos implementation (~1 ULP). The CUDA version uses cosf/sinf which are already the reduced-precision equivalents.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 15-30% overall kernel speedup. RoPE is compute-bound (sin/cos/pow dominate), and the trig calls are the primary bottleneck. Native versions reduce trig cost by 2-4x.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: In rope_yarn() at lines 34-35 of rope.cpp, change: cos_theta = sycl::native::cos(theta); sin_theta = sycl::native::sin(theta); Alternatively, use sycl::sincos() or native::sincos() if available for a single fused call. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 3.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Intel native sin/cos on Xe2 provides ~1 ULP accuracy which is sufficient for position embeddings. The CUDA version already uses equivalent fast-math functions.

optimization_opportunities.description: Replace sycl::pow(theta_scale, i0/2.0f) with sycl::native::exp2(sycl::native::log2(theta_scale) * (i0/2.0f)) in all four kernel variants. sycl::pow is an expensive multi-cycle operation. The exp2/log2 decomposition is mathematically equivalent and maps to faster hardware instructions on Xe2. The log2(theta_scale) term is constant per-kernel-invocation and could be precomputed on the host, reducing it to a single native::exp2 call per thread.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 10-20% overall kernel speedup. sycl::pow is one of the most expensive operations per thread, called at lines 65, 105, 152-172 (8 branches in rope_multi), 212, 216.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: 1. Precompute log2_theta_scale = log2f(theta_scale) on the host side in the launcher functions (rope_norm_sycl etc.) and pass as kernel argument. 2. In each kernel, replace sycl::pow(theta_scale, (float)i0/2) with sycl::native::exp2(log2_theta_scale * (float)i0 * 0.5f). For rope_multi, the theta_scale power is used in all 8 sector branches — precomputing log2_theta_scale eliminates redundant work. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 3.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Mathematically equivalent transformation. The precomputed log2 value is exact for power-of-2 theta_scales (common case). For non-power-of-2 values, the error is within 1-2 ULP which is negligible for position embeddings.

optimization_opportunities.description: Add [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(16)]] attribute to all 8 kernel launch lambdas (lines 251, 261, 283, 288, 314, 319, 349, 354). While not a correctness issue for RoPE (no sub-group operations are used), specifying SIMD16 ensures the compiler generates native-width code for Xe2 rather than potentially selecting SIMD32 which would reduce occupancy by 2x (fewer hardware threads per XVE).
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 5-15% improvement from better occupancy. Without the attribute, the compiler may choose SIMD32 (32 work-items per thread), which halves the number of hardware threads that fit per XVE on Xe2, reducing latency hiding.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Add [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(16)]] to each parallel_for lambda. Example: stream->parallel_for(nd_range<3>(...), [=](nd_item<3> item) [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(16)]] { ... }); Apply to all 8 parallel_for calls across rope_norm_sycl (2 calls), rope_neox_sycl (2), rope_multi_sycl (2), rope_vision_sycl (2). Ref: optimization_guide.md section 1.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: No sub-group operations are used, so this only affects occupancy and register allocation. No functional impact.

optimization_opportunities.description: Simplify 3D nd_range to 2D nd_range. All kernels use sycl::nd_range<3> with dimension 0 always being 1 (a DPCT migration artifact from CUDA dim3). Converting to nd_range<2> removes the trivial dimension, slightly reduces launch overhead, and makes the code clearer. Dimension mapping: current dim 1 (block columns) → new dim 0, current dim 2 (rows) → new dim 1.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Negligible performance improvement (<2%). Primary benefit is code clarity and maintainability.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: 1. Change nd_range<3>({1, num_blocks, nr}, {1, 256, 1}) to nd_range<2>({num_blocks, nr}, {256, 1}) at lines 239, 276, 305, 340. 2. Update kernel functions to accept nd_item<2> instead of nd_item<3>. 3. Update thread index computation: i0 = 2 * item.get_global_id(0), row = item.get_global_id(1).
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Purely mechanical refactoring. Well-defined mapping from 3D to 2D dimensions.

optimization_opportunities.description: Clean up DPCT artifacts: (1) Replace manual thread indexing (local_range*group+local_id) with get_global_id() at 8 locations, (2) Remove unconditional dpct::has_capability_or_fail(fp16) checks in rope_norm_sycl and rope_neox_sycl (lines 243, 280) — guard with if constexpr like rope_multi/vision already do, (3) Remove DPCT migration comments (lines 246-250, 256-259).
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Minor: removes per-launch device capability queries (~microseconds). get_global_id() may enable compiler optimizations vs manual index arithmetic.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: 1. Lines 46,52,86,92,128,132,196,200: replace item_ct1.get_local_range(N)*item_ct1.get_group(N)+item_ct1.get_local_id(N) with item_ct1.get_global_id(N). 2. Lines 243,280: wrap with if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, sycl::half>) like lines 309-311 and 344-346 already do. 3. Delete DPCT comment blocks.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Mechanical cleanup with no algorithmic changes.

kernels.estimated_current_efficiency: 55-65% — RoPE is compute-bound (sin/cos/pow operations dominate) and uses standard precision math functions where native versions would be significantly faster on Xe2. The work-group size (256) and coalesced access patterns are reasonable. No SLM or reductions needed. Main gains come from switching to native math functions.

kernels.name: norm SYCL kernels

launch_config.work_group_size: dynamic: WARP_SIZE (16) for ncols < 1024, device max_work_group_size for ncols >= 1024; rms_norm_back caps at 256
launch_config.global_size_expression: (nsamples, nchannels, nrows) for norm/rms_norm; (1, 1, num_groups) for group_norm; (1, 1, N) for rms_norm_back and l2_norm
launch_config.notes: All 5 kernels use 3D nd_range. All have [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] — good. Critical issue: rms_norm_f32 uses only WARP_SIZE (16) threads for ncols < 1024, while CUDA uses 256 threads — significant throughput loss for mid-range column counts (32-1023). group_norm uses 3D nd_range but only dimension 2 is meaningful.

strided_accesses: group_norm_f32: three separate passes over the same data (mean, variance, scale) — 3x memory traffic
memory_patterns.notes: All kernels use scalar float reads/writes. Consecutive threads access consecutive elements (coalesced via col = tid; col < ncols; col += block_size). norm_f32/rms_norm use calculate_offset<3> for strided source support. l2_norm_f32 uses explicit row*ncols multiply per access instead of pointer offset — extra ALU overhead. No sycl::vec usage anywhere.

slm_usage.slm_bytes: norm_f32: up to 64 * sizeof(float2) = 512 bytes; group_norm: up to 64 * sizeof(float) = 256 bytes; rms_norm: up to 64 * sizeof(float) = 256 bytes; rms_norm_back: 2 * 16 * sizeof(float2) = 256 bytes; l2_norm: up to 64 * sizeof(float) = 256 bytes
slm_usage.notes: SLM usage is minimal and well within the 64 KB per Xe-core limit. No bank conflicts detected — writes are one per sub-group, reads are coalesced within sub-group.

reduction_pattern.notes: Three DIFFERENT reduction implementations across five kernels: (1) norm_f32/rms_norm_f32 use clean sub-group API (sub_group.get_group_linear_id()) with ceil_div nreduce and local_space barrier. (2) group_norm_f32/l2_norm_f32 use old DPCT-migrated pattern with manual warp_id/lane_id, integer division nreduce (not ceil_div — potential bug), and group_norm uses GLOBAL barrier instead of local_space barrier. (3) rms_norm_back_f32 uses cleanest pattern with sub-group API + sycl::group_broadcast. None use sycl::reduce_over_group.

data_types.notes: FP32 throughout is appropriate for normalization numerical stability. norm_f32 uses sycl::float2 for combined mean+variance accumulation — register-efficient. rms_norm_back_f32 uses compensated (Kahan) summation for improved numerical accuracy (unless GGML_SYCL_RMS_BACK_FAST is defined).

functions: sycl::rsqrt (norm_f32 line 54, rms_norm_f32 line 198, rms_norm_back line 622, l2_norm line 242)
math_functions.notes: All kernels use standard sycl::rsqrt, not sycl::native::rsqrt. On Xe2, native::rsqrt is ~2x faster. CUDA uses rsqrtf() which maps to a fast hardware intrinsic. The rsqrt is called once per work-group (only thread 0 or broadcast result), so the absolute impact is small but switching to native is trivial.

hot_loops: norm_f32: accumulation loop (lines 27-31) iterates ncols/block_size times
norm_f32: write-back loop (lines 56-58) iterates ncols/block_size times
group_norm_f32: THREE passes — mean (lines 76-78), variance (lines 109-113), scale (lines 143-145)
loop_analysis.notes: No #pragma unroll on any hot inner loop in any kernel. CUDA uses compile-time template block_size which enables automatic unrolling. SYCL uses runtime block_size parameter which prevents compiler unrolling.

anti_patterns: group_norm_f32 uses GLOBAL barrier (item_ct1.barrier()) at lines 97, 132 instead of local_space barrier — unnecessary global memory fence overhead
group_norm_f32 has DPCT artifact comments at lines 88-96, 122-131 (DPCT1118, DPCT1065)
l2_norm_f32 has DPCT artifact comment at lines 228-231 (DPCT1118:3)
Dispatch functions have stale DPCT comments at lines 269-273, 309-313, 355-358, 395-398 (DPCT1049)
Three different reduction styles across five kernels — inconsistent code, harder to maintain and optimize
group_norm_f32 uses nwarps/WARP_SIZE (integer division) instead of ceil_div — inconsistent with norm_f32/rms_norm which use ceil_div
l2_norm_f32 uses explicit row*ncols multiply per access instead of pointer offset — based on outdated CUDA version
l2_norm_f32 is out-of-date with current CUDA: missing stride support for non-contiguous tensors
rms_norm_f32 uses only WARP_SIZE (16) threads for ncols < 1024 while CUDA uses 256 — poor occupancy
Missing CUDA fused rms_norm_multiply and rms_norm_multiply_add kernels — significant feature gap
group_norm_f32 may not handle batched input correctly — dispatches num_groups vs CUDA's num_groups * ne[3]
rms_norm_back_f32 is an inline 100+ line lambda instead of a separate function
Runtime block_size parameter prevents compiler loop unrolling across all kernels

optimization_opportunities.description: Fix group_norm_f32 global barrier to use local_space fence. Lines 97 and 132 use item_ct1.barrier() which includes an unnecessary global memory fence. Since the barrier only synchronizes SLM access, it should use item_ct1.barrier(sycl::access::fence_space::local_space). This is both a performance fix and a correctness alignment — the other kernels (norm_f32, rms_norm_f32, l2_norm_f32) already correctly use local_space barriers.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 5-15% speedup for group_norm_f32. Global barriers stall the memory pipeline until all global memory writes are visible, which is unnecessary when only SLM synchronization is needed. The impact is proportional to how often the barrier is hit (2x per kernel invocation).
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: At lines 97 and 132 of norm.cpp, change: item_ct1.barrier() to item_ct1.barrier(sycl::access::fence_space::local_space). This is a one-line change per occurrence. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 6.2 (avoid unnecessary synchronization).
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: The SLM writes at lines 87 and 121 are the only writes being synchronized. No global memory writes occur between SLM write and barrier. Other kernels in the same file already use local_space correctly.

optimization_opportunities.description: Unify all five kernels to use sycl::reduce_over_group instead of manual SLM-based cross-warp reduction. Currently three different reduction patterns are used, with group_norm and l2_norm using an older DPCT-migrated style that is less efficient. sycl::reduce_over_group(item.get_group(), val, op) handles the entire work-group reduction optimally with minimal barriers. This eliminates 20+ lines of manual reduction code per kernel and removes the nreduce calculation (and its ceil_div vs integer division inconsistency).
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 10-20% speedup across all norm kernels from reduced barrier overhead and optimal reduction tree. Also eliminates ~100 lines of duplicated reduction code and the inconsistency between ceil_div and integer division nreduce calculations.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: For each kernel: (1) Remove SLM local_accessor for inter-warp communication. (2) Replace warp_reduce_sum + SLM store + barrier + SLM read loop + warp_reduce_sum with single call: result = sycl::reduce_over_group(item.get_group(), partial, sycl::plus<float>()). For norm_f32 which reduces float2, do two separate reduce_over_group calls (one for mean, one for variance) or pack into float and reduce separately. For rms_norm_back_f32 which already uses the cleanest pattern, the change is still beneficial for consistency. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 3.4.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Need to verify reduce_over_group works correctly with all work-group sizes (16 to 1024). The small work-group path (WARP_SIZE=16) should work since reduce_over_group handles single-sub-group reductions. For group_norm which does two reductions, need to ensure both can use reduce_over_group independently. Test with representative models (LLaMA, GPT) to verify numerical equivalence.

optimization_opportunities.description: Increase rms_norm_f32 work-group size for ncols < 1024 from WARP_SIZE (16) to 256 threads. CUDA uses 256 threads for this path (norm.cu line 302-303). The current SYCL implementation uses only 16 threads per work-group, which provides terrible occupancy on Xe2 — only 1 hardware thread per XVE (1/8 capacity). For typical LLM dimensions like 768, 1024, 2048, this path may be hit or the boundary case matters. RMS normalization is one of the most frequently called kernels in transformer inference (applied before every attention and FFN layer).
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 2-4x throughput improvement for the small path (ncols < 1024). The larger work-group allows 16x more threads to cooperate on each row, dramatically improving memory bandwidth utilization for this memory-bound kernel. Even for the large path, ensuring the work-group size is reasonable (256-512 rather than device max 1024) may improve occupancy.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: At line 340 of norm.cpp, change the small-path work-group size from (1, 1, WARP_SIZE) to (1, 1, 256). The kernel code already handles arbitrary block_size via the col += block_size stride loop, so no kernel changes are needed — only the dispatch. However, the SLM allocation must now be provided (currently nullptr for the small path). Add local_accessor<float, 1> of size 256/WARP_SIZE = 16 floats. Apply the same fix to norm_f32 (line 255) and l2_norm_f32 (line 377) which also use WARP_SIZE for the small path.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: The kernel is already parameterized by runtime block_size and handles multi-warp reduction via SLM. The only risk is ensuring the SLM allocation is provided for the small path, which is a mechanical change.

optimization_opportunities.description: Add vectorized memory access (sycl::vec<float, 4>) to the accumulation and write-back loops in all norm kernels. Currently all loads and stores are scalar float, processing 1 element per thread per iteration. Normalization kernels are memory-bound (compute intensity ~2-4 ops/byte for rms_norm, well below the 27 ops/byte threshold), so maximizing memory throughput is critical.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 20-40% throughput improvement for memory-bound norm kernels. Vector loads reduce memory transactions by 4x for aligned data. For typical LLM hidden dimensions (4096, 8192) which are multiples of 4, this is safe and effective.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: For each hot loop (e.g., rms_norm_f32 lines 172-175), change from: float xi = x[col]; tmp += xi * xi; col += block_size; to: sycl::vec<float, 4> xv = *reinterpret_cast<const sycl::vec<float, 4>*>(&x[col*4]); tmp += xv[0]*xv[0] + xv[1]*xv[1] + xv[2]*xv[2] + xv[3]*xv[3]; Handle tail elements (ncols % 4 != 0) with scalar fallback. Apply to all accumulation and write-back loops. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 2.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Requires ncols to be a multiple of 4 for the vectorized path (fallback needed otherwise). Most LLM dimensions are multiples of 64+, so this is safe in practice. Need to ensure pointer alignment for reinterpret_cast.

optimization_opportunities.description: Replace sycl::rsqrt with sycl::native::rsqrt in all norm kernels (lines 54, 142, 198, 242, 622). While rsqrt is called only once per row (not per element), switching to native is trivial and removes any potential for the compiler to emit a slower standard-precision sequence. CUDA's rsqrtf() maps to hardware intrinsic automatically.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 1-3% — negligible per-call since rsqrt is called once per row, but free to implement and eliminates a minor inefficiency.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Replace sycl::rsqrt(x) with sycl::native::rsqrt(x) at 5 locations in norm.cpp. For l2_norm, also verify sycl::max usage is appropriate (sycl::max is already optimal). Ref: optimization_guide.md section 3.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: native::rsqrt provides ~1 ULP accuracy which is more than sufficient for normalization. The result is used as a scaling factor, not for further computation chains.

optimization_opportunities.description: Implement missing fused rms_norm_multiply and rms_norm_multiply_add kernels. CUDA has template variants rms_norm_f32<block_size, do_multiply=true> and rms_norm_f32<block_size, do_multiply=true, do_add=true> that fuse RMS normalization with element-wise multiply (and optionally add) in a single kernel pass. This avoids a separate element-wise kernel launch and halves memory traffic for the fused operation. In transformer inference, RMS norm is almost always followed by a scale multiply, making this fusion highly impactful.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 30-50% throughput improvement for the fused path. Eliminates one kernel launch + one full pass over the output data. For a 4096-element row, this saves 4096*4 = 16KB of memory traffic per row. With thousands of rows per inference step, this adds up significantly.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Add template parameters do_multiply and do_add to rms_norm_f32 kernel. When do_multiply is true, read an additional input pointer (scale) and multiply during the write-back loop: dst[col] = x[col] * inv_r * scale[col % scale_stride]. When do_add is true, also add a bias. Implement dispatch functions ggml_sycl_op_rms_norm_fused and ggml_sycl_op_rms_norm_fused_add. May need fastmodulo equivalent for broadcasting the scale across batch dimensions. CUDA uses fastmodulo from common.cuh for this.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: New feature implementation. Requires understanding the fastmodulo broadcasting pattern from CUDA. Needs new dispatch logic in the SYCL backend (ggml-sycl.cpp). May require changes to the op graph to detect and use the fused kernel.

optimization_opportunities.description: Clean up DPCT migration artifacts across all norm kernels: (1) Remove stale DPCT comments at lines 88-96, 122-131, 228-231, 269-273, 309-313, 355-358, 395-398. (2) Unify reduction style: convert group_norm and l2_norm from manual warp_id/lane_id pattern to sub-group API (matching norm_f32 and rms_norm patterns). (3) Fix nreduce inconsistency: use ceil_div consistently. (4) Simplify group_norm and l2_norm 3D nd_range to 1D where only dimension 2 is used.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Minor direct performance improvement. Primary benefit is code maintainability, consistency, and enabling further optimizations. The ceil_div fix may prevent edge-case bugs with non-standard work-group sizes.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: 1. Delete DPCT comment blocks (7 locations). 2. In group_norm_f32 and l2_norm_f32, replace warp_id = tid / WARP_SIZE; lane_id = tid % WARP_SIZE with auto sg = item_ct1.get_sub_group(); auto sg_id = sg.get_group_linear_id(); auto wi_in_sg = sg.get_local_linear_id(). 3. Change nwarps / WARP_SIZE to ceil_div(nwarps, WARP_SIZE) in group_norm (line 68) and l2_norm (line 233). 4. Convert nd_range<3>((1,1,N),(1,1,WG)) to nd_range<1>(N,WG) for l2_norm and group_norm.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Mechanical refactoring. The sub-group API pattern is proven working in norm_f32 and rms_norm_f32. The ceil_div change makes the code safer but shouldn't affect typical work-group sizes.

optimization_opportunities.description: Update l2_norm_f32 to match current CUDA implementation with stride support. The SYCL version is based on an older CUDA version that uses contiguous row*ncols addressing. Current CUDA (norm.cu lines 239-271) supports full 3D strided layout via stride_row, stride_channel, stride_sample parameters. The SYCL dispatch (ggml_sycl_op_l2_norm, lines 636-654) does not compute or pass stride information.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Correctness fix for non-contiguous tensors + minor ALU savings from removing row*ncols multiply. Not a performance-critical optimization since l2_norm is less frequently used than rms_norm.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: 1. Update l2_norm_f32 kernel to accept stride parameters and use calculate_offset<3> for source addressing (matching norm_f32 pattern). 2. Update ggml_sycl_op_l2_norm dispatch to compute and pass stride information from the tensor metadata. 3. Update grid dimensions from (1,1,nrows) to (nsamples, nchannels, nrows_per_channel) matching CUDA's (nrows, nchannels, nsamples) grid.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Requires careful mapping of tensor dimension ordering between CUDA and SYCL. The calculate_offset utility is already proven in norm_f32 and rms_norm_f32.

optimization_opportunities.description: Fix potential batch dimension bug in group_norm_f32 dispatch. SYCL dispatches num_groups work-groups (norm.cpp line 453), while CUDA dispatches num_groups * ne[3] work-groups (norm.cu line 449) to account for the batch dimension. If batched group normalization is used, the SYCL version may produce incorrect results.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Correctness fix — no performance change for single-batch inference. Enables correct multi-batch group normalization if needed.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: In ggml_sycl_op_group_norm (around line 453), change the number of work-groups from num_groups to num_groups * src0->ne[3]. Pass the additional batch dimension info to the kernel.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Simple dispatch fix. The kernel itself handles arbitrary group sizes, so only the grid size needs adjustment.

kernels.estimated_current_efficiency: 35-45% — Norm kernels are memory-bound but waste bandwidth through scalar accesses (no vectorization), have inconsistent and suboptimal reduction patterns (3 different styles, one using global barriers), use unnecessarily small work-groups for the small path (16 vs CUDA's 256), and are missing the critical fused rms_norm_multiply kernel that eliminates a full memory pass in transformer inference.

kernels.name: element_wise SYCL kernels

launch_config.global_size_expression: ceil_div(n, 256) * 256 for contiguous ops; product of dimensions for generic stride path; swiglu_oai uses 3D nd_range
launch_config.notes: All element-wise kernels use SYCL_ELEMENT_WISE_BLOCK_SIZE=256 with nd_range<1>, except swiglu_oai which uses nd_range<3> (DPCT artifact). No [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size]] specified on any kernel. ~25 unary ops, 5 fused GLU ops, plus acc_f32, arange, upscale, clamp, xielu, silu_back.

strided_accesses: generic stride path: per-element 4D address decomposition (i0/i1/i2/i3 + byte offset multiply)
memory_patterns.notes: All ops use scalar loads/stores — one element per work-item. Consecutive threads access consecutive elements for the contiguous fast path (coalesced). The generic stride path (unary_op_generic_kernel) performs expensive 4D address decomposition per element. No sycl::vec usage anywhere despite all ops being trivially vectorizable.

slm_usage.notes: No SLM needed — all ops are purely element-wise with no data sharing.

data_types.notes: All computation is FP32. Input/output types handled through casting. FP32 is appropriate for transcendental functions (gelu, silu, sigmoid, etc.) where half-precision could cause quality issues.

math_functions.notes: Inconsistent native math usage: silu and sigmoid correctly use sycl::native::exp, but gelu uses standard sycl::tanh, exp op uses standard sycl::exp, sin/cos use standard versions, log uses standard version. All should use sycl::native:: variants where precision allows. CUDA equivalents use __expf, tanhf, etc. which are fast-math by default.

loop_analysis.notes: No loops within kernels — each work-item processes exactly one element. The outer dispatch loop is the nd_range grid.

anti_patterns: All element-wise ops use scalar loads/stores — should use vec4 for 2-4x memory throughput improvement
Inconsistent native math: silu/sigmoid use native::exp but gelu/exp/sin/cos/log do not use native equivalents
Five separate GLU kernel bodies duplicate index math — CUDA uses a single template kernel with function pointer parameter
swiglu_oai uses 3D nd_range (DPCT artifact) while all other element_wise kernels use nd_range<1>
__dpct_inline__ artifacts should use standard inline or nothing
Generic stride path (unary_op_generic_kernel) performs expensive 4D address decomposition per element without fast-path detection for contiguous case
acc_f32 only supports 3D tensors (asserts dst->ne[3] == 1) while CUDA supports 4D
Missing upscale modes: SYCL only has nearest-neighbor, CUDA also has bilinear and bicubic

optimization_opportunities.description: Add vectorized loads/stores (sycl::vec<float, 4>) to all contiguous-path element-wise kernels. Currently all ~25 unary ops, 5 GLU ops, and other element-wise kernels process one scalar float per work-item. For memory-bound element-wise ops, vec4 loads can improve memory throughput by 2-4x by reducing memory transactions. Element-wise ops are the simplest case for vectorization since there are no inter-element dependencies.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 20-40% throughput improvement for memory-bound element-wise ops (most of them). Compute-heavy ops (gelu, silu, sigmoid) will see less improvement since they are closer to compute-bound.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Create a vectorized wrapper that loads 4 elements, applies the unary op to each, and stores 4 elements. The contiguous dispatch path (ggml_sycl_op_unary) can check alignment and n%4==0 to use vec4 path. Each work-item processes 4 elements instead of 1, reducing grid size by 4x. Handle tail elements with scalar fallback. Apply to both unary ops and GLU ops. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 2.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Element-wise ops have no inter-element dependencies, making vectorization safe. Need to handle non-aligned and non-multiple-of-4 element counts with scalar fallback.

optimization_opportunities.description: Use sycl::native:: variants consistently for all transcendental functions in element-wise ops. Currently silu and sigmoid correctly use sycl::native::exp, but many other ops use standard versions: gelu uses sycl::tanh (should be native::tanh or native::exp-based), exp op uses sycl::exp (should be native::exp), sin/cos use sycl::sin/sycl::cos (should be native::sin/native::cos), log uses sycl::log (should be native::log), sqrt uses sycl::sqrt (should be native::sqrt). On Xe2, native math functions are 2-4x faster than standard precision versions.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 10-30% speedup for compute-bound ops (gelu, sigmoid, tanh, exp, log, sin, cos). For memory-bound ops the improvement is smaller since compute is not the bottleneck. The gelu kernel (2x exp + tanh + multiply) benefits most from native math.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Replace in each kernel: sycl::tanh → sycl::native::exp-based tanh or direct native (if available), sycl::exp → sycl::native::exp, sycl::sin → sycl::native::sin, sycl::cos → sycl::native::cos, sycl::log → sycl::native::log, sycl::sqrt → sycl::native::sqrt. For gelu, the tanh can be rewritten as: t = native::exp(2*x); result = t/(t+1) (sigmoid-based form) which uses only native::exp. Ref: optimization_guide.md section 3.2.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Native math provides ~1 ULP accuracy which is sufficient for activation functions in LLM inference. silu/sigmoid already use native::exp successfully, confirming the precision is acceptable.

optimization_opportunities.description: Consolidate the 5 separate GLU kernel bodies (gated_op_fused_geglu, gated_op_fused_reglu, gated_op_fused_swiglu, gated_op_fused_geglu_erf, gated_op_fused_geglu_quick) into a single template kernel with a function pointer or constexpr-if parameter, matching CUDA's unified unary_gated_op_kernel<op> pattern. The 5 kernels duplicate the same index computation logic (i0, i1, row, col, x_offset, g_offset) and only differ in the activation function applied.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: No performance improvement — code quality and maintainability fix. Reduces ~150 lines of duplicated kernel code to ~40 lines. Makes it easier to add new GLU variants.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Create template: template<typename ActivationOp> void gated_op_fused_kernel(nd_item<1>, ..., ActivationOp op) with the common index math, then instantiate with lambda or functor for each activation (gelu, relu, silu, gelu_erf, gelu_quick). Update dispatch to use the template.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Mechanical refactoring. All 5 kernels already have identical control flow and only differ in one line (the activation function call).

optimization_opportunities.description: Convert swiglu_oai from 3D nd_range to 1D nd_range, matching all other element_wise kernels. The 3D nd_range is a DPCT migration artifact — the kernel is logically 1D (one element per thread). This simplifies thread index computation and removes unnecessary dimensions.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Negligible performance improvement (<2%). Primary benefit is code consistency and maintainability.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Change nd_range<3> to nd_range<1>. Update thread index computation from 3D decomposition to simple get_global_id(0). Grid size = ceil_div(total_elements, 256) * 256.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Mechanical refactoring. The kernel is logically 1D with no dimensional dependencies.

optimization_opportunities.description: Clean up __dpct_inline__ artifacts throughout element_wise.cpp. Replace with standard C++ inline keyword or remove entirely (the compiler inlines small functions automatically). This is a DPCT migration artifact that reduces code portability.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: No performance improvement — code quality fix for portability and readability.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Replace all instances of __dpct_inline__ with inline or remove the annotation entirely. The functions are small enough that the compiler will inline them regardless.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Mechanical cleanup with no functional changes.

optimization_opportunities.description: Add contiguous fast-path detection for the generic stride kernel (unary_op_generic_kernel). The generic path performs expensive 4D address decomposition (i0/i1/i2/i3 + byte offset multiply) per element. For contiguous tensors, this decomposition is unnecessary — a simple linear index suffices. Detecting contiguity at dispatch time and routing to the fast path avoids this overhead.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 5-15% for ops that go through the generic path with contiguous tensors. The address decomposition adds ~10 ALU ops per element (4 divisions + 4 modulos + 4 multiplies + additions) which is significant for simple ops like relu or neg.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: At dispatch time (in ggml_sycl_op_unary or equivalent), check if src and dst have contiguous strides (ne[i] * nb[i] == nb[i+1] for all i). If contiguous, use the existing fast path. If non-contiguous, use the generic path. This check is already partially done for some ops but not consistently applied.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Adding a dispatch-time check has no risk. The fast path already exists and is proven correct.

optimization_opportunities.description: Feature gap: acc_f32 only supports 3D tensors (asserts dst->ne[3] == 1) while CUDA supports 4D with ne13/s13 parameters. This limits the operations that can run on the SYCL backend.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: No performance improvement — feature completeness fix.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Add ne13 and s13 parameters to the acc_f32_sycl kernel. Remove the assert(dst->ne[3] == 1) check and add an outer loop or grid dimension for the 4th dimension.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Straightforward extension of existing 3D logic to 4D.

optimization_opportunities.description: Feature gap: upscale kernel only implements nearest-neighbor interpolation. CUDA supports bilinear (with and without antialiasing) and bicubic modes. This limits model compatibility for vision and image processing workloads.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: No performance improvement — feature completeness fix for vision model support.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Implement bilinear and bicubic interpolation modes in the upscale kernel, matching CUDA's implementation. The dispatch should select the mode based on the op parameters.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Bilinear and bicubic are more complex algorithms requiring multi-element reads with interpolation weights. Need careful testing against CUDA reference output.

kernels.estimated_current_efficiency: 60-70% — Element-wise kernels are simple and already reasonably well-implemented. The main performance wins come from vectorized loads (2-4x memory throughput for bandwidth-bound ops) and consistent native math usage (2-4x faster transcendentals for compute-bound ops like gelu/silu). Code quality improvements (GLU dedup, DPCT cleanup) are beneficial but don't affect performance significantly.

kernels.name: convert (dequantize) SYCL kernels

launch_config.work_group_size: 256 for generic dequantize_block and convert_unary; 32 for Q4_0/Q4_1/Q4_K/IQ*/MXFP4 specialized kernels; 64 for Q2_K/Q3_K/Q5_K/Q6_K; WARP_SIZE for q4_0_reorder
launch_config.sub_group_size: Only q4_0_reorder specifies [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]]; all others have no sub-group size attribute
launch_config.global_size_expression: Generic: ceil_div(k, 2*256) work-groups; K-quant/IQ: k/QK_K work-groups; convert_unary_nc: 3D grid (ne02*ne03, ne01, ceil_div(ne00, 256))
launch_config.notes: All kernels use nd_range<3> with dimensions 0 and 1 set to 1 (except convert_unary_nc which uses all 3 dimensions). Small work-group sizes (32) for specialized quant kernels are dictated by the per-block element count (QK_K=256, 32 threads handle 256/32=8 elements each). The generic dequantize_block uses SYCL_DEQUANTIZE_BLOCK_SIZE=256 matching CUDA's CUDA_DEQUANTIZE_BLOCK_SIZE=256.

strided_accesses: Generic dequantize_block writes to y[iybs + iqs] and y[iybs + iqs + y_offset] with y_offset=qk/2 for qr>1 — strided writes for interleaved quant formats
memory_patterns.notes: All dequantize kernels process 2 output elements per thread (via dfloat2/float2). Reads from quantized blocks are coalesced within sub-groups (consecutive threads read consecutive quant indices). Writes are coalesced for qr==1 types but strided by qk/2 for qr>1 types. The reorder variants (q4_0_reorder, q4_K_reorder, q6_K_reorder) use separated d/qs memory layout for better access patterns. No sycl::vec loads used anywhere.

slm_usage.slm_bytes: Q4_K and Q4_K_reorder: 12 bytes (scale_local_acc for scale unpacking)
slm_usage.notes: Only Q4_K variants use SLM (12 bytes for scale buffer). All other dequantize kernels are SLM-free. The CUDA version accesses scales directly from device memory (no shared memory) — the SYCL version added SLM for better locality on Intel GPUs.

reduction_pattern.notes: No reductions — each thread independently dequantizes a fixed subset of elements from one quantization block.

data_types.notes: The dequantize kernels use dfloat2 which is sycl::half2 when GGML_SYCL_F16 is defined, otherwise sycl::float2. When targeting fp16 output, computing in half avoids fp32→fp16 conversion overhead. CUDA has a heavily optimized Q8_0→FP16 kernel using half2 arithmetic and shared memory (dequantize_block_q8_0_f16) that SYCL lacks entirely.

math_functions.notes: Dequantize kernels use no transcendental math — only integer bit manipulation, multiplies, and adds. No optimization opportunities for native math.

hot_loops: convert_unary_nc: loop over i00 with stride work_group_size * num_groups (line 503) — handles large ne00 that exceeds max SYCL global range
Specialized Q4_0/Q4_1 kernels: implicit loops (each thread handles 8 quantization blocks × 32 elements)
loop_analysis.notes: convert_unary_nc has #pragma unroll on its loop. Specialized kernels have compile-time-known iteration counts enabling auto-unrolling. Generic dequantize_block has no loops (2 elements per thread, one-shot).

anti_patterns: Generic dequantize_block is contiguous-only (flat k parameter) — CUDA's generic version supports non-contiguous tensors natively via stride parameters (ne00/ne01/ne02/s01/s02/s03)
All non-reorder kernels use nd_range<3> with dimensions 0,1 = 1 — DPCT artifact, should use nd_range<1>
Missing optimized Q8_0→FP16 kernel — CUDA has dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 with shared memory and half2 arithmetic for 2-3x speedup
dpct::has_capability_or_fail(fp16) called unconditionally on every launch — wastes time on capability query per kernel dispatch
__dpct_inline__ artifacts in dequantize.hpp kernel functions

Non-contiguous (NC) support gap: SYCL only has fp16 NC output via convert_unary_nc_sycl for F32/BF16 input; CUDA has NC variants for all basic quant types (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0) and all output types (fp16, fp32, bf16)
Missing to_bf16_sycl_t typedef and to_fp32_nc_sycl_t, to_bf16_nc_sycl_t dispatch functions
Generic dequantize_block processes only 2 elements per thread — could process more to amortize thread launch overhead
convert_unary_nc_sycl has global range downsample workaround (downsample_sycl_global_range) adding complexity — SYCL limitation for large tensor dimensions
Missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size]] on all kernels except q4_0_reorder — may cause suboptimal SIMD width on Xe2

optimization_opportunities.description: Implement optimized Q8_0→FP16 dequantize kernel matching CUDA's dequantize_block_q8_0_f16. CUDA has a heavily optimized kernel that uses shared memory to load entire Q8_0 blocks, then dequantizes using half2 arithmetic with 2048-element alignment. The SYCL version uses the generic scalar dequantize_block path which processes only 2 elements per thread. Q8_0 is the most common intermediate quantization format used during inference (activations are often Q8_0 quantized for GEMM).
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 2-3x speedup for Q8_0→FP16 dequantization. The CUDA optimized kernel uses shared memory for coalesced reads, half2 vectorized arithmetic, and processes 2048 elements per block vs the generic kernel's 512 elements per block (256 threads × 2 elements).
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Port CUDA's dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 to SYCL: (1) Allocate SLM buffer of size (CUDA_Q8_0_NE_ALIGN/sizeof(int) + WARP_SIZE) × sizeof(int). (2) Cooperatively load Q8_0 blocks into SLM using coalesced reads. (3) Barrier. (4) Each thread reads d (scale) and qs (quantized values) from SLM, dequantizes using sycl::half2 multiply. (5) Use [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]]. Need to handle tail blocks with need_check template parameter. Register the optimized kernel in ggml_get_to_fp16_sycl for GGML_TYPE_Q8_0.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Shared memory staging pattern is well-understood. The half2 arithmetic requires SYCL fp16 support which is already used elsewhere. Need alignment handling for non-2048-aligned element counts.

optimization_opportunities.description: Add [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] to all dequantize kernel launch paths. Currently only q4_0_reorder has this attribute (line 148). All other kernels (~20 launch sites) lack it, which may cause the compiler to select SIMD32 instead of SIMD16 on Xe2, halving occupancy. The dequantize kernels don't use sub-group operations explicitly, but specifying the native SIMD width ensures optimal register allocation and occupancy.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 5-15% throughput improvement from better occupancy. Without the attribute, Xe2 may use SIMD32 (2 elements per hardware thread) instead of SIMD16, reducing the number of hardware threads per XVE and worsening latency hiding for these memory-bound kernels.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Add [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE)]] to the lambda in every parallel_for call in convert.cpp. There are approximately 20 launch sites. This is a mechanical change with no algorithmic impact.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: No sub-group operations are used, so this only affects SIMD width selection. No functional impact. Already proven working on q4_0_reorder.

optimization_opportunities.description: Support non-contiguous (NC) dequantization for quantized types in SYCL. CUDA's generic dequantize_block natively supports NC tensors via stride parameters (ne00/ne01/ne02/s01/s02/s03) and 3D grid indexing. SYCL's generic dequantize_block only supports contiguous tensors (flat k parameter). SYCL's NC support is limited to convert_unary_nc_sycl which only handles F32/BF16→FP16 conversion. This means quantized tensor reshaping or non-contiguous views must materialize contiguous copies before dequantization on SYCL.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Eliminates extra copy operations for non-contiguous quantized tensors — up to 2x speedup for those paths by avoiding the contiguity materialization step. Also enables new dispatch paths (get_to_fp32_nc_sycl, get_to_bf16_nc_sycl) matching CUDA's API surface.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Modify dequantize_block to accept ne00/ne01/ne02/s01/s02/s03 stride parameters matching CUDA's version. Use 3D nd_range for the NC path: grid = (ceil_div(ne00, 2*block_size), ne01, ne02*ne03). Compute source offset as i03*s03 + i02*s02 + i01*s01 + i00/qk. Compute dest offset as ((i03*ne02 + i02)*ne01 + i01)*ne00 + iybs + iqs. Add dispatch functions get_to_fp32_nc_sycl, get_to_bf16_nc_sycl, and extend get_to_fp16_nc_sycl to support quantized input types.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Multi-dimensional indexing must be carefully mapped. The CUDA version is proven correct and can serve as reference. Need to handle the downsample_sycl_global_range workaround for large tensor dimensions.

optimization_opportunities.description: Remove unconditional dpct::has_capability_or_fail(fp16) checks from all dequantize launch functions. These capability queries are called on every kernel dispatch, adding microseconds of overhead per launch. The fp16 capability should be checked once at device initialization, not per-dispatch. Most dequantize kernels don't even require fp16 capability (they output float).
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Reduces per-dispatch latency by ~1-5 microseconds. For batched inference with many small dequantize calls, this adds up. More importantly, this is incorrect for float output — the fp16 check is a DPCT artifact that doesn't apply to fp32 dequantization.

kernels.name: binbcast (binary broadcast) SYCL kernels

launch_config.global_size_expression: 3D adaptive: block_dims = (min(ne2*ne3, cap), min(ne1, cap), min(hne0, 128)) where cap fills to 128; fallback 1D: ceil_div(ne0*ne1*ne2*ne3, 128) when z-dim exceeds 65535
launch_config.notes: Two kernel variants: k_bin_bcast (3D grid) and k_bin_bcast_unravel (1D fallback). Block size is 128 matching CUDA. The 3D grid packs dimensions 2 and 3 into the z-axis using integer division (ne2*ne3 packed). The dimension 0 uses hne0 = max(ne0/2, 1) which halves the grid in dimension 0. Missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size]] on both kernel launch paths. Fallback condition only checks z-dim > 65535, while CUDA checks both y AND z — potential bug for large ne1.

strided_accesses: src1 broadcast: i10 = i0 % ne10 causes non-contiguous access when ne10 < ne0
src0/src1 stride-based addressing via s01/s02/s03 and s11/s12/s13
memory_patterns.notes: Innermost loop iterates over dimension 0 with stride equal to total threads in dimension 0. Consecutive threads access consecutive elements in src0 and dst (coalesced). src1 access is coalesced only when ne10 >= ne0 (no broadcast in dim 0); otherwise the modulo causes irregular access. All loads/stores are scalar — no sycl::vec usage.

slm_usage.notes: No SLM used. Pure element-wise operations with no inter-thread data sharing.

reduction_pattern.notes: No reductions — each thread computes one or more output elements independently.

data_types.notes: All binary ops compute in float regardless of input/output types. Supports 6 type combinations: f32/f32/f32, f16/f16/f16, f16/f32/f16, i32/i32/i32, i16/i16/i16. SYCL has i32 and i16 support that CUDA lacks. CUDA additionally supports f16/f32/f32 which SYCL does not.

math_functions.notes: No transcendental math — only add, sub, mul, div operations. div uses standard float division. No optimization opportunities for native math.

hot_loops: k_bin_bcast inner loop (line 44-48): iterates ne0/(block_dims[2]*block_nums[2]) times — handles multiple elements per thread in dimension 0
Dimension collapse loop (lines 127-139): host-side, iterates up to 3 times to collapse non-broadcast dimensions
loop_analysis.notes: The inner loop in k_bin_bcast cannot be unrolled since ne0 is runtime. The loop body is simple (one load from each src + one op + one store). k_bin_bcast_unravel has no loop — one element per thread.

anti_patterns: Uses plain integer % and / for broadcast index computation (i1%ne11, i2%ne12, i3%ne13, i0%ne10, i/(ne2*ne1*ne0) in unravel) — CUDA uses fastdiv/fastmodulo with multiply-high (2-3 cycles vs 20-30 cycles for integer division on GPU)
DPCT artifact: dpct::has_capability_or_fail(fp16) called on every launch
DPCT artifact: stale DPCT1049 comment at lines 240-245
Missing [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size]] on both launch paths
Fallback condition only checks block_nums[0] > 65535 — CUDA checks both y AND z grid limits; missing y check is a potential correctness bug for large ne1
Missing fused multi-source op support — CUDA's variadic template fuses up to 8 add operations into a single kernel launch, eliminating redundant memory traffic
Missing repeat_back kernel — CUDA has k_repeat_back for the inverse of repeat
s00 is GGML_UNUSED instead of GGML_ASSERT(s00 == 1) — CUDA asserts this for safety

optimization_opportunities.description: Replace plain integer % and / with fast division/modulo for broadcast index computation. CUDA uses fastdiv/fastmodulo which precomputes magic numbers and uses multiply-high + shift (2-3 cycles) instead of hardware integer division (20-30 cycles on GPU). In binbcast, every thread executes 3-4 modulo operations (i1%ne11, i2%ne12, i3%ne13, i0%ne10) and the unravel kernel adds 3-4 integer divisions (i/(ne2*ne1*ne0) etc.). This is the single largest performance gap vs CUDA for this kernel.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 15-40% speedup depending on tensor dimensions. For small-element broadcast ops (where compute per element is minimal: add/sub = 1 FLOP), the division overhead dominates. The unravel kernel (1D fallback) is worst affected — 7+ divisions per thread vs 0 with fastdiv.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Implement a SYCL fastdiv utility matching CUDA's: precompute (mp, L, divisor) triple on host for each ne value, pass as kernel parameters. Replace % with fastmodulo and / with fastdiv in both k_bin_bcast and k_bin_bcast_unravel. The host-side init_fastdiv_values() computes: L = ceil(log2(d)), mp = 2^(32+L)/d + 1. The device-side fastdiv uses __umulhi(n, mp) >> L. On SYCL/Intel, use sycl::mul_hi for the multiply-high operation.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: The fastdiv algorithm requires careful handling of edge cases (divisor = 1, power of 2 divisors). CUDA's implementation is proven correct. Need to verify sycl::mul_hi behavior matches __umulhi for unsigned 32-bit multiply-high.

optimization_opportunities.description: Implement fused multi-source binary broadcast operations matching CUDA's ggml_cuda_op_fused_add. CUDA uses variadic templates (src1_ptrs...) with C++17 fold expressions to fuse up to 8 add operations into a single kernel launch. This eliminates N-1 kernel launches and N-1 redundant reads/writes of the destination tensor for N fused operations. In transformer inference, multiple bias additions or residual connections can be fused.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 30-50% throughput improvement for fusible add chains. For a chain of N adds, reduces memory traffic from 3N passes (read src0 + read src1 + write dst per add) to N+2 passes (read src0 + N src1 reads + 1 write). Also eliminates N-1 kernel launch overheads.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Add variadic template parameter pack src1_ptrs to k_bin_bcast and bin_bcast_sycl. Use C++17 fold expression: result = (..., (result = bin_op(result, (float)src1s[i_src1 + i10]))). Add ggml_sycl_op_fused_add dispatch function that detects fusible add chains in the op graph and batches them. Requires modifications to ggml-sycl.cpp dispatch logic to detect fusible patterns.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Requires op graph analysis to detect fusible patterns. The variadic template approach requires careful handling of different tensor shapes and broadcast patterns across fused operations. Need to ensure all fused sources have compatible broadcast dimensions.

optimization_opportunities.description: Fix the fallback condition to check both y and z grid dimension limits, matching CUDA. Currently SYCL only checks block_nums[0] > 65535 (z-dimension equivalent) but not block_nums[1] (y-dimension). CUDA checks both: block_nums.z > 65535 || block_nums.y > 65535. If ne1 is very large (>65535 * block_dims[1]), the SYCL kernel could fail or produce incorrect results.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Correctness fix — prevents potential failures with large ne1 dimensions.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Change the condition at line 221 from: if (block_nums[0] > 65535) to: if (block_nums[0] > 65535 || block_nums[1] > 65535). This ensures the 1D fallback kernel is used whenever any grid dimension exceeds SYCL limits.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Simple conditional change. The unravel fallback kernel already handles arbitrary dimensions correctly.

optimization_opportunities.description: Add [[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(16)]] to both kernel launch paths (k_bin_bcast and k_bin_bcast_unravel). Without this attribute, the compiler may choose SIMD32 on Xe2, halving occupancy for these memory-bound kernels.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: 5-10% from better occupancy and latency hiding.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Add the attribute to both parallel_for lambdas at lines 232 and 251.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: No sub-group operations are used. Only affects SIMD width selection.

optimization_opportunities.description: Implement repeat_back kernel. CUDA has k_repeat_back for the inverse of repeat (summing elements that were repeated back to the original size using atomicAdd). SYCL binbcast does not have this, which may cause fallback to CPU or incorrect behavior for backward pass of repeat operations.
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Feature completeness — enables SYCL backward pass for repeat operations without CPU fallback.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Port CUDA's k_repeat_back kernel: for each output element, use atomicAdd to accumulate contributions from all repeated input elements. Use sycl::atomic_ref<float, ...> for the atomic operation. The kernel iterates over repeat dimensions and accumulates.
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Atomic operations on float require sycl::atomic_ref with memory_order::relaxed. Need to verify Intel GPU support for float atomics. The atomic approach may have contention for small output tensors.

optimization_opportunities.description: Clean up DPCT artifacts: remove dpct::has_capability_or_fail(fp16) check, delete stale DPCT1049 comment, replace __dpct_inline__ on op functions in binbcast.hpp. Also add GGML_ASSERT(s00 == 1) to match CUDA's safety check instead of GGML_UNUSED(s00).
optimization_opportunities.expected_improvement: Minor: removes per-dispatch capability query overhead. Code quality improvement.
optimization_opportunities.implementation_notes: Remove dpct::has_capability_or_fail blocks (lines 225-226, 246-247). Delete DPCT comment (lines 240-245). Replace __dpct_inline__ with inline in binbcast.hpp. Change GGML_UNUSED(s00) to GGML_ASSERT(s00 == 1).
optimization_opportunities.risk_notes: Mechanical cleanup. The s00 assert adds a safety check that CUDA already has.

kernels.estimated_current_efficiency: 50-60% — Binary broadcast kernels are memory-bound but waste significant cycles on expensive integer division for broadcast index computation (CUDA uses fastdiv for 10x cheaper division). Missing fused multi-source support leaves significant throughput on the table for common add chains. The dimension collapse optimization and 3D grid mapping are well-implemented, matching CUDA. Missing repeat_back is a feature gap.
